packages.label: דִּבּוּר וְהֵיכַל הַמֶּלֶךְ
packages.label_en: Speech and the Palace of the King
packages.reason: The sole connected component in Torah #194 contains two nodes: אדני and דבור. The Rebbe explicitly declares: 'אדני, בחינת הדבור' — the Divine Name אדני (associated with the mouth and speech, as in 'אדני שפתי תפתח', Psalm 51:17) is a bechina of speech. This is the conceptual core of the entire Torah: speech (דבור) is the היכל המלך (palace of the King), the sacred domain that belongs to God alone. דבור is dominant (it is the hub around which the teaching revolves), while אדני is the Divine-Name expression of that same reality. The polarity is 'good' because this cluster describes holy speech — the King's own palace — as distinct from the degraded honor-seeking that the Torah condemns. The human who distinguishes himself from animals through speech (גדר האדם = דבור) participates in this holy domain only insofar as he speaks truthfully and humbly before the King.
